findings: Baseline and selective prompts frequently volunteer names before requested; names are therefore reported separately from other clues.
Baseline 015 speculates about the pet, repairs and photography; selective 015 calls keeping the turtle a hobby. The lexical wrong-value rate does not capture these unsupported assertions.
Brief 001 invents a pet named Felix instead of stating turtle; lexical coverage loses the pet but the wrong-value metric misses the invented pet name.
Oracle 005 shifts to the players pet and invents its hobby; oracle 015 describes the pet as a mechanic. The latter gets incorrect lexical job credit.
Oracle 011 invents that the teacher teaches English; oracle 017 infers personality from a pet. Both exceed the card.
Several answers assert the work city instead of residence (e.g. baseline 003 and 009); lexical city matching cannot distinguish those relations.
Baseline early full reveals 004 and 019 omit city. Full-record coverage is kept separate.
Core card retrieval is sufficient for the controlled study, with these explicit scorer limitations. Only truth-preserving reviewed contrasts may be extracted.
